item.content:encoded: Hah! That little "thread deleted" at the end was such a cheeky little nod. I love it. item.content:encoded:
First off: I love it. The idea of the Foundation working with "gifted" kids (which reads like a reality bender early warning/innoculation program/program for the children of Foundation employees to make sure their kids aren't accidentally anomalous) is just delightfully weird and works on so many levels. The writing sells it, too. The choices of slightly stilted vocabulary really drives home the point that the author is from an educated background.

Some notes: the replies at the end feel… meh? After the excellent main post the two replies just don't feel quite as thought out. Also, instead of LARP, I think ARG would possibly fit better? Dunno.

The collapsible at the end doesn't feel like it adds anything. I get you're going for "Foundation saw and deleted this to cover it up" but it just ends up looking like a broken collapsible to me. Maybe reword it to something hinting at the user being the Foundation mod that's deleting the thread and clicking it changes it to "Thread flagged for deletion" or something along those lines.

Tl;dr: absolutely excellent. +1

item.title: Re: +1
item.content:encoded:
This was totally my feeling. There are a lot of shady, esoteric, incomprehensible things the Foundation certainly is involved in, and showing how this looks to outsiders has a lot of potential. There also is a disturbing element of realism with the Foundation using random people as test subjects (D-Class source?) or sleeper agents or something when you look at just how many times a major country's government has blatantly experimented on its own people.

Edit: Okay so the Foundation is just making people compliant, I accidentally missed a line.

While there are a lot of things I could say that are positive about this, I wanna focus on one bit of it that I really loved - the Foundation being presented as this esoteric, occult thing. This is like the Foundation as the Operator from Marble Hornets and I love it. I'd love to see more stories that paint the Foundation in a similar light.
